pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word in Bring the clothes inside is the verb? (1 mark)
   A. inside
   B. Bring
   C. clothes
   D. the

2. Why is reading fluently important? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the book smaller
   B. It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   C. It hides mistakes
   D. It ends the lesson early

3. Which is a mistake in reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Looking up at the audience
   B. Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   C. Practising first
   D. Pausing at full stops

4. How many full stops are needed in: The sky is dark. Rain is coming. (1 mark)
   A. One
   B. Three
   C. None
   D. Two

5. In the story of Otieno, what caused his burn? (1 mark)
   A. He fell from a tree
   B. He played with a dog
   C. He touched the handle of the hot pot
   D. He ate hot food

6. Which answer is a full sentence for: Why did the pot tip over? (1 mark)
   A. The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   B. Because
   C. Handle
   D. Otieno

7. How are words arranged in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. In alphabetical order
   B. By the number of letters
   C. By colour
   D. By size of the word

8. What is a word puzzle used for? (1 mark)
   A. Running
   B. Painting
   C. Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   D. Cooking

9. What should you put after a starting word such as First? (1 mark)
   A. A question mark
   B. A colon
   C. A comma
   D. Nothing

10. Which sentence is a metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. The classroom was as busy as a beehive.
   B. The classroom was like a beehive.
   C. The classroom was busy.
   D. The classroom was a beehive.

11. What should you do when you use a simile or metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. Use hurtful comparisons
   B. Never explain it
   C. Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   D. Use very many in one sentence

12. What does the proverb Look before you leap advise a writer of a story about a careless pupil? (1 mark)
   A. Think before acting
   B. Never look
   C. Be careless
   D. Run fast

13. Why should you plan before writing a story? (1 mark)
   A. To organise your ideas
   B. To make it longer
   C. To finish early
   D. To avoid a title

14. What is a customer? (1 mark)
   A. A person who buys
   B. A kind of shop
   C. A type of money
   D. A person who sells only

15. In The seller counts the money, what is the predicate? (1 mark)
   A. The
   B. counts the money
   C. money only
   D. The seller

16. Which word joins two ideas that contrast? (1 mark)
   A. and
   B. because
   C. but
   D. so

17. Who should you call for a sick animal? (1 mark)
   A. A tailor
   B. A veterinary doctor
   C. A shopkeeper
   D. A driver

18. In choral recitation, the group (1 mark)
   A. reads silently
   B. says the poem together at the same pace
   C. writes the poem
   D. sings only

19. What is community service? (1 mark)
   A. Playing only
   B. Selling goods
   C. Helping the community without pay
   D. Sleeping

20. What is a motion in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. The statement the teams discuss
   C. A song
   D. A dance

21. Which interjection shows sudden understanding? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Oops
   C. Aha
   D. Ouch

22. Why are interjections used more in speech than in formal writing? (1 mark)
   A. They are long
   B. They show quick feelings in speech
   C. They are illegal in writing
   D. They are difficult

23. Which is a polite phrase to ask someone to repeat? (1 mark)
   A. Say it again now
   B. What did you say?
   C. Stop talking
   D. Could you repeat that, please?

24. Which is the last part of a telephone conversation? (1 mark)
   A. Greeting
   B. Asking for a favour
   C. Giving your name
   D. Saying goodbye

25. What should you do first when a call is answered? (1 mark)
   A. Greet politely
   B. Ask for money
   C. Hang up
   D. Shout

26. Which is a part of a form? (1 mark)
   A. Poem
   B. Ending song
   C. Title
   D. Riddle

27. What is a digital form? (1 mark)
   A. A form on a tree
   B. A form made of clay
   C. A paper airplane
   D. A form filled in on a device

28. What does format mean for a form? (1 mark)
   A. What it costs
   B. How old it is
   C. How it is arranged on the page
   D. Who wrote it

29. Why is it important to obey leaders? (1 mark)
   A. It is boring
   B. It is a game
   C. It keeps order, peace and safety
   D. It makes noise

30. What should the title of an instruction chart do? (1 mark)
   A. Tell what the task is
   B. Hide the task
   C. Give a joke
   D. Be blank

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write a four-line dialogue between two friends deciding what to do in their free time. Use two interjections. (4 marks)

32. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)

33. What is a vocabulary bank and why is it useful? (2 marks)

34. List the two verbs in the sentence: The teacher counted the votes and announced the winner. (2 marks)

35. Correct this paragraph: it was a cold morning in nyeri the children wore sweaters scarves and socks (4 marks)

36. List the six elements of a story. (3 marks)

37. Put the steps in order: (a) Finally, serve. (b) First, boil water. (c) Next, add tea leaves. (3 marks)

38. Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question. (3 marks)

39. Put in order: shillings the pays customer fifty (3 marks)

40. Explain what a dialogue is. (2 marks)

41. Choose one proverb and explain its meaning. Then describe a real situation at school where it would apply. (5 marks)

42. Write the plural of each English noun: plate, tomato. (2 marks)

43. Write a short speech of four sentences about caring for a goat. Use at least two prepositions. (5 marks)

44. What is a verb? Give two examples. (2 marks)

45. Write three sentences describing where things are in your classroom. Use a different preposition in each. (3 marks)

46. Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters. (2 marks)

47. Give two rules for looking after class library books. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Bring
   Bring shows the action.

2. B — It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   Fluent reading helps meaning.

3. B — Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   Speed that is too fast loses meaning.

4. D — Two
   There are two sentences, so two full stops.

5. C — He touched the handle of the hot pot
   He moved closer and touched the handle, and the pot tipped.

6. A — The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   A full sentence has a subject and a verb and gives the reason.

7. A — In alphabetical order
   Dictionaries use alphabetical order.

8. C — Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   Puzzles help pupils remember words.

9. C — A comma
   We usually put a comma after First at the start of a sentence.

10. D — The classroom was a beehive.
   A metaphor says one thing is another.

11. C — Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   Clear and kind comparisons work best.

12. A — Think before acting
   It would fit a story where carelessness causes trouble.

13. A — To organise your ideas
   A plan gives your story a clear shape.

14. A — A person who buys
   A customer buys goods or services.

15. B — counts the money
   The predicate tells what the subject does.

16. C — but
   But shows contrast.

17. B — A veterinary doctor
   Veterinary doctors treat animals.

18. B — says the poem together at the same pace
   Choral means together.

19. C — Helping the community without pay
   Community service benefits others.

20. B — The statement the teams discuss
   The motion is the topic.

21. C — Aha
   Aha shows realising something.

22. B — They show quick feelings in speech
   Formal writing usually uses full sentences.

23. D — Could you repeat that, please?
   Please and could show politeness.

24. D — Saying goodbye
   Calls end with a goodbye.

25. A — Greet politely
   A greeting begins the call.

26. C — Title
   A form has a title.

27. D — A form filled in on a device
   Digital forms are filled on phones or computers.

28. C — How it is arranged on the page
   Format is the layout.

29. C — It keeps order, peace and safety
   Obeying fair leaders keeps everyone safe.

30. A — Tell what the task is
   The title names the task.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines with speaker names, colons, a clear topic and two suitable interjections.
   Working / marking points: One mark for names and colons, one mark for suitable content, one mark for each interjection.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a class list of words on one theme. It helps pupils remember and use new words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the use.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: counted, announced
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb. Teacher, votes and winner are nouns.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: It was a cold morning in Nyeri. The children wore sweaters, scarves and socks.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four corrections: capitals at the start, Nyeri, the full stops and the commas.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending.
   Working / marking points: Award 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, and 1 mark for two or three.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: b, c, a
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct position.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: The customer pays fifty shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the words in order, one for the capital and one for the full stop.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, shown with each speaker's name and words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for speakers.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct proverb with a sensible meaning and a matching situation, for example A stitch in time saves nine means fix small problems early, such as mending a small tear in a uniform before it grows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the proverb, two marks for the meaning and two marks for a clear situation.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: plates, tomatoes
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two prepositions, for example Give the goat water beside the food. Build a shed behind the house. Do not put a heavy load on it. Call the veterinary doctor if it is sick.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for correct prepositions.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example The board is in front of the class. My bag is under my desk. The teacher stands beside the door.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible reason.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Turn pages gently, never write in them, return them on time, keep them clean (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.
